acceptance_checks: A worktree created while the coordinator sits on a feature branch is cut from the default branch, proven by the new branch's tip equalling the default branch tip (git rev-parse) and `git diff <default>...<new branch>` being empty at creation.
An existing worktree at the recorded path is reused unchanged.
An unresolvable default branch fails with a named reason instead of silently cutting from HEAD.
A task PR created this way carries no mirror file belonging to another goal.
shiki runner claude alone produces a correctly based worktree; no operator git worktree command is needed.
non_goals: Changing what the loop syncs onto the branch

findings.detail: git diff main...HEAD includes ~25 commits of intervening merged goals' mirror records and code (PRs #181-#186, Contract PR #182 plan) because this worktree was cut from a stale local main before this fix existed. This is a symptom of the exact bug the task fixes for future worktrees, not a defect in the change. MergeGate derives its base from origin/main, so it is a rebase concern for PR #187 rather than a code correctness issue. Non-blocking.
findings.title: Diff carries large foreign .shiki mirror state due to stale-local-main base

findings.detail: resolve_default_branch_ref fixes the dispatch worktree base, but shiki_loop.py:437 `git rev-list --count main..HEAD` reads the same stale local main. The repair packet explicitly scopes this out (shiki_loop.py is outside this task's locks) and records it as a separate finding. Correctly deferred; noted for tracking.
findings.title: Sibling stale-ref bug in shiki_loop.py:437 remains

scope:
scripts/shiki_runtime.py ensure_physical_worktree runs `git worktree add` from the coordinator's cwd, so a task branch is cut from whatever branch the coordinator happens to be on. The loop's own comments already assert the opposite — shiki_loop.py:481 states a task branch 'is cut from main' and that a multi-task goal's DAG 'already rides in from main'. Cutting from a coordinator branch carrying other goals' mirror state put 19 foreign task files, 2 foreign goal files and 33 unlisted ledgers into the first PR's diff, measured at 56 MergeGate blocking reasons. Cut explicitly from the configured default branch and fail with a named reason when it cannot be resolved.

REPRODUCIBILITY — what this task removes. On 2026-07-27/29 a single task was driven from Goal to PR twice (#179, merged; #181, open at the time of writing). The loop's judgments were autonomous; the plumbing between them was not. Seven manual interventions were required, and this task removes one of them.
  Manual step removed: creating each task worktree from origin/main by hand.
  Observed: ensure_physical_worktree runs git worktree add from the coordinator's cwd, so a branch is cut from whatever the coordinator sits on; doing that on a branch carrying three goals' mirror state produced 56 MergeGate blocking reasons on the first PR, while shiki_loop.py:481 asserts branches are cut from main.
  Reproducible when: shiki runner claude alone produces a task branch based on the default branch, with no operator git worktree command and no foreign goal's mirror state in the diff.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_runner_claude.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Cut task worktrees from the default branch
